expectations.text: The survey evidence is used to justify the audience-presence score but is not allowed to override the funding floor.
expectations.evidence: Section 3 ties the survey directly and only to the scoring of presence/reachability: "Podcast's value-5 on audience presence and reachability is direct evidence: 200-signup survey, top answer, buyer named the exact 2–3 shows." The funding floor is then treated as a separate, independently-checked gate: the starved-family promotion lists condition (3) as "budget clears the family's floor *by concentrating on known-good shows* (math below)" — i.e. the floor is satisfied by concentration math, not waived because the evidence is strong. expectations.text: The survey evidence is used to justify the audience-presence score but is not allowed to override the funding floor.
expectations.evidence: The survey is used correctly as audience-presence evidence: 'Use those as the anchor picks — survey data beats my guesswork every time' and 'Confirm the actual named shows from your survey (don't skip this — it's better data than my shortlist)' — so the 200 respondents justify which shows have real audience presence. However, no explicit funding floor is defined as a separate, non-overridable constraint.
